messages:
Alex: kicking off a small canary for the new rate-limit policy (global default 10rps -> 8rps). Sending 10% of traffic to canary now. monitoring: latency, 429s, quota errors. ping if you see customer impact. :eyes:

Priya: quick q — does the canary apply to dedicated tenants or only hosted API keys? need to know for customer comms.

Marcos: only hosted API keys for this canary. dedicated pools are excluded unless an admin opt-in. we used canary tag `rl-canary-2026-03` on the routing config.

Jen: FYI set up eval hooks — compare 1m 50p latency, 429 rate, and tokens billed. alerts wired to #eng-sre and ticket auto-created if >0.5% spike in 429s.

support-bot: Automated alert — elevated 429 rate detected for `rl-canary-2026-03` at 2026-03-15T14:08:54Z. 429 rate = 0.72% (baseline 0.1%). Affected customers: tenant-a, tenant-c. See runbook: https://runbook.internal/redwood/rate-limits

Sam: seeing customer report from tenant-a: reproducible with their batch job. Repro steps they sent: 1) open websocket stream 2) send 20 parallel requests within 1s 3) expect 200 but got 429 with header `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0`. logs: `request_id=abc123 status=429 route=/v1/completions key=sk-live-***`.

Alex: can you paste the full request headers and the `x-rw-*` header values? also check if KV cache warmed for that model — small seq lengths shouldnt hit this.

Sam: pasted logs —
```
request_id=abc123 host=api.redwood.dev route=/v1/completions method=POST status=429
x-rw-rate-limit-limit=8
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining=0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset=7
x-client-tenant=tenant-a
```

Marcos: that looks like the canary policy applied. Their job bursts >8rps so it's expected. two options: 1) increase per-tenant quota via admin override for tenant-a; 2) roll canary back while we assess burst handling.

Jen: prod metrics show overall 429 rate still low, but tenant-a and tenant-c are noisy. I'm +1 on pausing canary until we tweak burst window (short TTL on `x-rw-rate-limit-reset` maybe too aggressive).

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T14:05:22Z — routing config update `rl-canary-2026-03` -> 10% traffic. Commit: gh/infra#4821.

Alex: decision call: pause canary and rollback routing tag to previous config. rollback window = 30m. Marcos, can you run rollback? put a note in #incidents once done.

Marcos: running rollback now. command:
```
infractl routing rollback --tag rl-canary-2026-03 --to-tag rl-default-2026-02 --confirm
```

ops-runbook-bot: Rollback checklist — notify customers, unflip canary flag, re-evaluate quotas, run smoke tests. Link: https://runbook.internal/redwood/rate-limits#rollback

Sam: after rollback I ran the tenant-a job (same pattern) and they no longer hit 429s. headers show `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining=6`.

Priya: let's draft a KB note for tenant-a and tenant-c: explain bursty jobs need batching or client-side rate-limit backoff. also offer temporary quota bump if they have a commit to change behavior.

Jen: follow-ups: 1) add canary exclusion for tenants with scheduled batch jobs (heuristic by client-agent header), 2) add a grace-burst bucket for <500ms bursts, 3) update telemetry to include per-tenant burst percentile.

Alex: thanks all. action items pinned: Marcos -> confirm rollback and post link to rollback commit; Priya -> KB draft and customer comms; Jen -> telemetry + burst policy proposal; Sam -> collect repro logs and support ticket ids. I'll keep the change flagged in infra and schedule a 1h postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Support ticket created: S-2026-512. Assigned to Sam.

Marcos: rollback complete. routing state: reverted to `rl-default-2026-02`. commit gh/infra#4827. posted in #incidents.

Alex: closing thread for now, will reopen if we re-run canary. appreciate the quick responses. :rotating_light:
